items.title: Geometric regularity at a point of a locally finite type scheme over a field is equivalent to smoothness there
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and a point x, the lemma proves that geometric regularity at x is equivalent to smoothness of X over k at x (statement lines 2543-2550). One direction is immediate: localizing to an affine chart, smoothness over k survives arbitrary field extensions and makes each of the Noetherian rings involved regular (proof lines 2559-2563). The converse is the substantive direction and is a purely inseparable trick: taking the residue field K at x, which is finitely generated over k, one finds a finite purely inseparable extension k' such that the compositum k'K is separable over k'; because the prime lifted to k' tensor A is the unique prime over the original one, its residue field is exactly that compositum, so regularity of the base changed local ring plus separability makes k' to A' smooth at the lifted prime, and smoothness descends back along the purely inseparable field extension (proof lines 2565-2582). The claim is H2: three cited algebra inputs, but the choice of the purely inseparable extension and the uniqueness of the prime above are what make the argument work.
